newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles says its silver output rose 7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Penoles says its silver output rose 7 pct in 1996.

text.p: Mexican mining firm Penoles said on Wednesday that its silver production during 1996 was about seven percent higher than during 1995.
"We increased production by about seven percent," company director Jaime Lomeli told reporters in this western city.
Lomeli said production was about 1,800 tonnes or 55 million silver ounces. He added that the production was worth roughly $300 million.
Last year's silver production set a record high for the company, the world's largest silver producer with about 11 percent of world output, Lomeli said.
Penoles' gold output for 1996 was about 200,000 ounces, worth about $80 million.
Comparative figures for 1995 were not available.
The company was able to boost production largely because of increased output from its Fresnillo mine in Zacatecas state and the La Cienega mine in Durango state, he said.
Penoles will invest about $200 million in capital expenditures this year, he said, mostly in exploration projects.
He added that the company was also continuing its exploratory work in Peru and Argentina.
